headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: aci can egress CRM/email data while argo-workflows can act on unverified outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use direct function calls or MCP, and argo-workflows consumes REST/GRPC inputs; if aci’s outputs are passed into workflow parameters or files, prompt-like content could steer downstream behavior. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF aci output is copied into an Argo workflow parameter or artifact without sanitization
IF a shared MCP or filesystem bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for fields passed from aci to argo-workflows
Strip instructions and markup from aci outputs before workflow ingestion
Require human review for any workflow step derived from free-text output
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent payloads

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; argo-workflows has allowlisted egress and handles artifacts/parameters. If aci forwards sensitive records into workflow inputs, those data can leave the original boundary and be retained in artifacts. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF aci sends CRM, email, or support data into an Argo artifact or parameter
IF the allowlist permits the destination used by argo-workflows
mitigations: Minimize fields exported from aci to only non-sensitive identifiers
Disable artifact capture for sensitive workflow steps
Review Argo egress allowlist before enabling the pair
Set short retention on workflow artifacts
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering on inter-agent payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API access, while argo-workflows orchestrates REST/GRPC-driven jobs. If both are pointed at the same mutable external systems, they can race on shared records or workflow state. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so conflict risk is real but not proven high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same CRM, calendar, or workflow-backed resource
IF no external lock or idempotency key is enforced
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer for each resource
Use idempotency keys on all writes
Serialize overlapping jobs during rollout
Check for existing records before updates
requires-engineering: add distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and argo-workflows can execute parameterized jobs. If argo treats aci’s output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated recommendation can cascade into automated downstream actions. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so the unsafe default is plausible.
conditions: IF argo-workflows consumes aci output as a job parameter or decision input
IF no validation step checks aci output before execution
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any workflow action
Require schema validation on aci outputs
Limit argo steps to read-only dry runs initially
Add human approval for destructive jobs
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds and rollback hooks

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, and support data, which may include regulated personal data, while argo-workflows processes artifacts and parameters with allowlisted egress. The profiles do not document residency, retention, or DPA alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not specific enough for high severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed from aci into argo-workflows artifacts
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between agents
Block regulated fields from workflow artifacts
Document retention settings for both systems
Confirm residency and DPA coverage before rollout
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
